chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man ate from prey that was caught by one in Ihram, while he (the man) was not in Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: So let the one who is not in Ihram eat from it, and there is nothing upon him. Indeed, the ransom (fidyah) is upon the one in Ihram.

key_terms.حَلَالٌ: one not in Ihram (free from consecration)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: one in Ihram (state of consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a non-pilgrim eating game caught by a pilgrim in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the principle of individual liability in Islamic jurisprudence, establishing that the penalty for hunting while in Ihram rests exclusively on the pilgrim who committed the act, not on the consumer. It highlights the distinction between the prohibition of consumption for the muhrim and the permissibility for the halal, reinforcing the Shia legal view that fidyah is tied to the specific state of ritual restriction rather than the nature of the game itself. This ruling is foundational in discussions of 'urf (customary practice) and the transfer of ownership in pre-modern Arabian contexts.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A man attains from a prey caught by one in Ihraam, and he is not in Ihraam’. Heasws said: ‘So let the one who is not in Ihraam eat from it, and there would be nothing upon him. But rather, the ransom is upon the one in Ihraam’.
en.sarwar: 7. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who in the state of Ihram kills a prey and one who is not in the state of Ihram eats it. He (the Imam) said, ‘One who is not in the state of Ihram can eat it and there is not anything on him but ransom is upon one who is in the state of Ihram/”
